info.title: OrbitGuard API
info.summary: Constellation resilience studio for the КосмоХакатон 2026 case
info.description:
Loads `cosmo-A-1.0` scenarios, simulates a constellation over its time grid, routes traffic from client sites to a gateway, and reports availability, outages and per-satellite criticality.

**Conventions.** Times are seconds from the start of the run (`t_s`), angles are degrees, distances kilometres, fractions are 0…1 (not percent). Keys are `snake_case`, matching the official case format.

AvailabilitySample.title: AvailabilitySample
AvailabilitySample.description:
Per-instant availability flags — what the timeline strip under the globe draws.

Three states, not two: `visible_no_route` is the whole point of the case, and
collapsing it into "no service" would hide the difference between "no
satellite overhead" and "satellite overhead but the mesh cannot reach the
gateway".

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.description: Fraction 0…1 of instants with a satellite in view

availability.title: Availability
availability.description: Fraction 0…1 of instants with a route to a gateway

site_profile.title: Site Profile
site_profile.description: Surroundings profile applied to this site, if any

effective_mask_deg.title: Effective Mask Deg
effective_mask_deg.description: The elevation mask the site actually saw: scenario mask or higher

masked_share.title: Masked Share
masked_share.description: Fraction 0…1 of instants a satellite cleared the scenario mask but the site's surroundings hid every one

CompareResponse.title: CompareResponse
CompareResponse.description:
Side-by-side view: what changed, and what it bought.

`changed_parameters` is the case's explicit requirement that a comparison
shows the changed parameters, not only the resulting numbers.

ConfigModel.title: ConfigModel
ConfigModel.description:
Overrides applied to a base scenario before a run.

`failures` and `gateway_outages` replace the scenario's lists when present
and leave them untouched when absent, so the panel can own the full list
without needing add/remove verbs.

`sites` sets a site's surroundings; `null` for a site clears the block its
scenario file carried; sites not named keep whatever they had.

The environment block is separate from the design block on purpose: the case
says variants are compared at a fixed altitude, ISL range and elevation mask,
so touching those marks the run as a sensitivity study rather than a design
variant, and every response echoes the effective environment back.

EphemerisResponse.title: EphemerisResponse
EphemerisResponse.description:
Positions over the whole horizon, for the globe's animation.

At the official grid this is ~1 MB uncompressed and ~324 KB gzipped for a
full day, so it ships in one response; `step_s` can coarsen it further when
the client would rather interpolate.

GatewayDependencyModel.title: GatewayDependencyModel
GatewayDependencyModel.description:
How narrow the network's exit to the ground is.

Named by the organisers as one of the two things an engineer looks for first
(alongside long outages). With a single gateway the question is how many
satellites ever deliver to it and how much of the day rests on the busiest.

JobStatusModel.title: JobStatusModel
JobStatusModel.description: Progress for the one operation slow enough to need it.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: Rank on the worst-served client (matches the case's per-client target) or on the mean across clients (what the organisers suggested at the Q&A)

method.title: Method
method.description: Move one angle at a time from several starting points, or enumerate the full grid. The grid costs coarse_steps ** free_axes full-day simulations and samples each angle far more coarsely for the same budget

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: Plain-language conclusion, including the honest negative case where the target is unreachable by phasing alone

OutageWindowModel.title: OutageWindowModel
OutageWindowModel.description:
A gap with no route.

`leading`/`trailing` mark gaps touching the ends of the horizon: their true
length is unknown, so they are reported apart from `max_bounded_outage_s`,
which is the number worth comparing between variants.

ParameterDiff.title: ParameterDiff
ParameterDiff.description: One parameter that differs between the compared variants.

PlaneBoundsModel.title: PlaneBoundsModel
PlaneBoundsModel.description:
Search space for one plane.

A `null` range means the parameter is **locked**: the engineer pins what the
real project has already fixed — a launch window, an agreed RAAN slot — and
the optimizer works around it. Without locks a recommendation is just a
number that ignores the constraints that actually bind.

PlaneConfigModel.title: PlaneConfigModel
PlaneConfigModel.description: Omitted fields keep the scenario's value — the panel sends only what it moved.

satellite_ids.title: Satellite Ids
satellite_ids.description: Restrict the sweep to these satellites; defaults to every one that flies

RouteTimelineResponse.title: RouteTimelineResponse
RouteTimelineResponse.description: Every instant's route for one client — what the route inspector scrubs through.

RunRequest.title: RunRequest
RunRequest.description:
Run a scenario, either one we already hold or one supplied inline.

Supplying `scenario` inline keeps the jury's "load a file and run it" path to
a single request, with no import step to fail in between.

SatelliteImpactModel.title: SatelliteImpactModel
SatelliteImpactModel.description:
How much the network loses without this satellite.

`worst_availability_drop` is measured on the *worst-served* client, not the
average, because the 90% target is judged per client: a satellite whose loss
costs one village 9 points and the others nothing is critical, and an average
would bury it.

SatelliteStateModel.title: SatelliteStateModel
SatelliteStateModel.description:
Position in both frames.

`lat_deg`/`lon_deg`/`alt_km` is what the globe consumes directly; the
Earth-fixed cartesian triple is kept because it is what `geometry.py`
actually produces, and a technical reviewer can check our conversion against
the module's own output without re-deriving it.

ScenarioDetail.title: ScenarioDetail
ScenarioDetail.description: Everything the configuration panel and globe need to draw an unrun scenario.

ScenarioSummary.title: ScenarioSummary
ScenarioSummary.description: One row in the scenario picker.

SensitivityRequest.title: SensitivityRequest
SensitivityRequest.description: Sweep one environment parameter to find where the target starts to hold.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: Lowest swept value at which every client meets the target, when one exists

environment_modified.title: Environment Modified
environment_modified.description: True when the run changed altitude/ISL range/elevation mask, which makes it a sensitivity study rather than a comparable design variant

site_conditions_active.title: Site Conditions Active
site_conditions_active.description: True when at least one ground site models terrain, buildings or altitude that raise its horizon above the scenario mask

SiteConditionsModel.title: SiteConditionsModel
SiteConditionsModel.description:
What surrounds one ground site — see `engine.site_conditions`.

A named profile supplies a default local mask; `mask_deg` overrides it,
`azimuth_mask` adds a horizon profile as `[azimuth_deg, elevation_deg]`
pairs, and `altitude_m` lifts the site off the sphere. The effective mask is
the higher of the scenario's mask and the local one, so conditions can only
remove links, never add them.

SiteProfileModel.title: SiteProfileModel
SiteProfileModel.description: A named starting point for a site's surroundings, with its rationale.

masked_satellites.title: Masked Satellites
masked_satellites.description: Per site: satellites above the scenario mask that its surroundings hide

SnapshotResponse.title: SnapshotResponse
SnapshotResponse.description: One instant of the network, fully described.

ValidationReport.title: ValidationReport
ValidationReport.description: Result of a dry-run check, so the UI can report before it commits.
